title: Stein factorization of a proper morphism to an affine scheme
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $X\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{s}\operatorname{Spec}A$ be its Stein factorization [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization], $B=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Then: (i) the ring map $A\to B$ is integral (every element of $B$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $A$); (ii) $q$ is proper; (iii) $q$ has geometrically connected fibres; in particular for every $t\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] (in particular nonempty), hence so is the subspace $q^{-1}(t)\subseteq X$, which $X_t$ maps homeomorphically onto.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Theorem 37.53.5 (Tag 03H2, label theorem-stein-factorization-general, line 15290), for $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ affine, where $S'=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(f_*\mathcal O_X)=\operatorname{Spec}H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$ (its (4)); (i) is its (2) through the affine case, (iii) is its (1) (geometrically connected with Stacks' convention that connected spaces are nonempty)

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $S\xleftarrow{s}S' = \operatorname{Spec}B$ for the relative-spectrum factorization supplied by [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization]. The preceding universal factorization lemma (Tag 03GY) applies because a proper morphism is universally closed and quasi-separated. It gives that $q:X\to S'$ is universally closed, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and surjective, that $s$ is integral, and that $q_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{S'}$ with $S'=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(f_*\mathcal O_X)$.

The morphism $q$ is separated by cancellation from the separated proper composite $s\circ q=f$ [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation], and it is locally of finite type because $s\circ q=f$ is locally of finite type and locally finite type is permanent under this composition [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Tag 03GY already gives that $q$ is universally closed. Combining universal closedness, separatedness and finite type is exactly properness, so $q$ is proper.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 37.53.5 (Tag 03H2), lines 15312--15321; Morphisms Lemma 03GN (used in the preceding factorization proof)

proof.text: The universal factorization lemma already identifies $s$ as integral and $S'$ as $\operatorname{Spec}H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$; over the affine base this is the induced integral ring map $A\to B$. Equivalently, the exact Mathlib leaf [lem-weil-pbc-stein-integral-global-sections] applies via `AlgebraicGeometry.isIntegral_appTop_of_universallyClosed` at Proper.lean:138.

To prove geometric connectedness, replace the base by $S'$ using $q_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{S'}$ from Tag 03GY; since $S'=\operatorname{Spec}B$ in the Stein factorization, the replaced situation has $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=B$. For a point $s\in S'$ apply the etale criterion Tag 03GZ: it suffices to check connectedness after every affine etale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S',s)$. Properness is preserved by this base change [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Writing $U=\operatorname{Spec}R'$, Tag 02KH (the proper special case of its quasi-compact quasi-separated flat-base-change lemma) gives $H^0(X_U,\mathcal O_{X_U})=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)\otimes_B R'=B\otimes_B R'=R'$, so the fibre over $u$ is in the normalized situation of [lem-weil-pbc-stein-normalized-fibre-idempotent].

source.place: Proof of Theorem 37.53.5 (Tag 03H2), lines 15321--15334; Lemma 03GZ; Cohomology Lemma 02KH

proof.text: The normalized affine situation is handled by the formal-functions/idempotent argument of Tag 03H2. The theorem on formal functions identifies the completed local ring at $s$ with the inverse limit of the global sections on the infinitesimal neighbourhoods $X_n$. A nontrivial idempotent on the fibre lifts compatibly through these neighbourhoods, producing a nontrivial idempotent in the completed local ring, which is impossible because that ring is local. The fibre is therefore connected and nonempty, by [lem-weil-pbc-stein-normalized-fibre-idempotent]. This proves that every geometric fibre of $q$ is connected.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 37.53.5 (Tag 03H2), lines 15334--15357; Cohomology Lemma 02OD and Derived Categories Lemma 0G7X

proof.text: Finally, [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies the underlying space of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_t$ with the topological inverse image $q^{-1}(t)$ by a homeomorphism (Stacks Schemes Lemma 26.18.5, Tag 01K1). Hence connectedness and nonemptiness of $X_t$ give the final topological assertion.
